_about: Codepoint range catalog for scan-hidden-unicode.py and sanitize-content.py. Each band lists a Unicode range that is invisible, direction-altering, or visually misleading in normal Latin-script instruction text. 'severity' drives the scanner's default fail threshold (critical+high fail by default; medium+low fail only under --strict; benign never fails). 'strip_level' tells the sanitizer when to remove the band (minimal < standard < aggressive). 'legitimate_use' documents why a band is NOT always an attack — read it before tightening severity, because the emoji bands (FE0F, ZWJ) false-positive on every README that uses emoji.
_threshold_note: Fail threshold is a scanner policy, not a catalog field: default fails on critical+high, --strict additionally fails on medium+low. Sanitizer uses strip_level: minimal strips only critical, standard adds high+medium, aggressive adds low. Benign is never stripped or failed unless explicitly forced.
_replace_note: Optional 'replace_with' (a 'U+XXXX' code point) makes the sanitizer substitute that character instead of deleting the band. It is set on bands a reader sees as a break or a blank (line/paragraph separators, NEL, VT/FF, FS-RS, the spacing Hangul fillers): deleting those would fuse the words either side ('end<LS>begin' -> 'endbegin'), and a newline would make the forged line real, so they flatten to U+0020. Write code points as 'U+XXXX' strings, never literal characters.

bands.name: Bidirectional overrides + embeddings
bands.members: LRE U+202A, RLE U+202B, PDF U+202C, LRO U+202D, RLO U+202E
bands.legitimate_use: Effectively never in source/config/instruction files. The Unicode bidi algorithm prefers isolates (U+2066-2069) for legitimate mixed-direction text; overrides are the Trojan Source vector (CVE-2021-42574). Treat any occurrence in CLAUDE.md/SKILL.md/source as hostile.
bands.attack: Trojan Source: reorders rendered glyphs so a human reviewer sees different text than the compiler/LLM tokenizer parses. Hide an instruction after what looks like the end of a line.

bands.name: Bidirectional isolates
bands.members: LRI U+2066, RLI U+2067, FSI U+2068, PDI U+2069
bands.legitimate_use: Genuinely used to wrap mixed-direction runs (e.g. an Arabic name inside English prose, or an identifier in scraped web content). Common in text fetched from the web. Suspicious — but not automatically hostile — inside hand-authored English instruction files.
bands.attack: Same reordering primitive as overrides, subtler. Pairs FSI/PDI to visually relocate a clause.

bands.name: Directional marks
bands.legitimate_use: Used to fix weak-directional punctuation in mixed-script text. Benign in genuinely multilingual documents; noise in pure-ASCII instruction files.
bands.attack: Minor reordering of adjacent neutral characters; usually a supporting actor, not the payload.

bands.name: Arabic letter mark
bands.legitimate_use: Legitimate in Arabic-script text. Out of place in English-only config.
bands.attack: Directional control reused outside Arabic context.

bands.name: Zero-width space
bands.legitimate_use: Occasionally inserted by word processors / web content for line-break hints. Effectively never needed in source or instruction files.
bands.attack: Invisible separator: splits a keyword to evade naive string filters, or pads hidden text. Renders as nothing.

bands.name: Zero-width non-joiner
bands.legitimate_use: Required in Persian, Arabic, and some Indic scripts to control ligature joining. Do NOT strip from genuinely multilingual content. Suspicious only in pure-Latin text.
bands.attack: Invisible filter-evasion / steganographic padding, same as ZWSP.

bands.name: Zero-width joiner
bands.legitimate_use: Load-bearing in emoji sequences (family / profession / flag emoji) and Indic scripts. Stripping it corrupts emoji and Devanagari. Whitelisted by default — this is the character that makes a naive scanner false-positive on every emoji.
bands.attack: Theoretically abusable as an invisible separator, but the false-positive cost of flagging it outweighs the rare attack. Flag only under --strict, never strip below aggressive.

bands.name: Word joiner + invisible math operators
bands.members: WJ U+2060, FUNCTION APPLICATION U+2061, INVISIBLE TIMES U+2062, INVISIBLE SEPARATOR U+2063, INVISIBLE PLUS U+2064
bands.legitimate_use: The invisible math operators have niche use in MathML. None belong in instruction or config files.
bands.attack: Invisible glue/separators for hidden-text smuggling and filter evasion.

bands.name: Soft hyphen
bands.legitimate_use: A hyphenation hint, invisible unless a renderer breaks the line exactly there (Unicode 18.0 section 23.2). Common in scraped web text (­) for German, Dutch or Finnish, but no orthography requires it, so deleting it loses nothing. high rather than medium for that reason: unlike ZWNJ, no script depends on it.
bands.attack: The ZWSP filter-evasion primitive: 'ad<SHY>min' renders as 'admin' while a string match for 'admin' misses it. Default_Ignorable_Code_Point, so most renderers draw nothing.

bands.name: Combining grapheme joiner
bands.legitimate_use: Blocks canonical reordering of combining marks and separates letter pairs for collation (Unicode 18.0 section 23.2.4) - scholarly Hebrew, some transliteration. Never needed in ordinary prose or instruction files.
bands.attack: A zero-width, Default_Ignorable mark with no glyph: splits keywords ('ad<CGJ>min') and pads hidden payloads like ZWSP, riding invisibly on the preceding letter.

bands.name: Mongolian vowel separator
bands.legitimate_use: Required in Mongolian orthography: it selects the final form of a following a/e, so stripping it changes how genuine Mongolian text is shaped. Script-specific like ZWNJ, hence medium + aggressive - the standard strip level promises not to corrupt real multilingual text.
bands.attack: A zero-width format character since Unicode 6.3 (a space separator before), so current renderers draw nothing while older regex engines and trim() routines still treat it as whitespace - a splitter that filters disagree on.

bands.name: Khmer inherent vowels
bands.members: KHMER VOWEL INHERENT AQ U+17B4, KHMER VOWEL INHERENT AA U+17B5
bands.legitimate_use: Invisible marks kept for phonetic transcription only; the Unicode NamesList says their use in other contexts is discouraged. Ordinary Khmer text never contains them.
bands.attack: Default_Ignorable combining marks with no glyph: an invisible separator inside a keyword, the same as ZWSP.

bands.name: Hangul choseong/jungseong fillers
bands.members: HANGUL CHOSEONG FILLER U+115F, HANGUL JUNGSEONG FILLER U+1160
bands.legitimate_use: Placeholders inside conjoining-jamo sequences for incomplete or archaic syllables. Modern Korean uses precomposed syllables and never needs them. Deleted, not replaced: inside a syllable they are zero-width.
bands.attack: Letters (Lo) that are Default_Ignorable: they pass word-character and identifier checks yet draw nothing, so they can sit inside a word or stand as an invisible name.

bands.name: Hangul filler
bands.legitimate_use: A compatibility filler from legacy Korean encodings; modern text has no use for it.
bands.attack: A letter (Lo), so word-character and identifier checks accept it, but fonts draw it as a space-width blank - it has been used as an invisible JavaScript variable name to hide a backdoor parameter. Replaced with a space rather than deleted: a reader sees a gap there, and deletion would fuse the words either side.

bands.name: Halfwidth Hangul filler
bands.legitimate_use: Halfwidth compatibility form of U+3164; no use in modern text.
bands.attack: Same as U+3164: a letter that renders as a blank. Replaced with a space for the same reason.

bands.name: Line and paragraph separators
bands.legitimate_use: Unambiguous line and paragraph separators (Unicode 18.0 section 23.2; section 5.8 Newline Guidelines). Turn up in text pasted from some editors and inside JSON/JavaScript strings, but plain-text files break lines with LF, and hand-authored instruction files have no reason to carry them.
bands.attack: Structure forgery: UAX #14 class BK (mandatory break), line terminators to JavaScript and Python's str.splitlines(), and a model may read them as a new line - while many editors and terminals render them as nothing or keep the text inline. 'ok<LS>=== FORGED ===' puts a forged marker on a line of its own for the model, not for the reviewer. Flattened to a space: deletion would fuse the words either side, and a newline would make the forged line real.

bands.name: Next line (NEL)
bands.legitimate_use: The EBCDIC newline (Unicode 18.0 section 23.1; section 5.8). Essentially absent from modern UTF-8 text; when it does appear it is usually Windows-1252 text mis-decoded as Latin-1 (0x85 is an ellipsis there), which is worth a look anyway.
bands.attack: UAX #14 class NL and a str.splitlines() boundary, but a C1 control that most viewers draw as nothing: the U+2028 forged-line primitive in another code point.

bands.name: Vertical tab and form feed
bands.legitimate_use: Visible to a raw-byte review: most code editors draw a control-character glyph, and vim / bat --show-all show ^K / ^L. Form feed is a legitimate page break in RFC-style text and GNU source, and some word-processor exports use VT for a manual line break. Hence medium (--strict only), not high.
bands.attack: UAX #14 class BK and str.splitlines() boundaries, and terminals move the cursor down on them: a line-oriented consumer splits where a rendered view showed one line.

bands.name: Information separators FS, GS, RS
bands.members: FS U+001C, GS U+001D, RS U+001E (INFORMATION SEPARATOR FOUR, THREE, TWO)
bands.legitimate_use: Record delimiters for legacy data formats; no use in text files (JSON forbids them unescaped). Covered alongside VT/FF because Python's str.splitlines() treats them as line boundaries too.
bands.attack: Terminals draw nothing for them, yet str.splitlines() starts a new line at each one: the forged-line primitive in the C0 range.

bands.name: BOM / zero-width no-break space
bands.legitimate_use: Legitimate as a byte-order mark at the VERY START of a file. Anywhere else it is a zero-width no-break space with no modern purpose. The scanner notes position; a mid-file occurrence is the suspicious one.
bands.attack: Mid-stream invisible separator; also used to confuse parsers.

bands.name: Variation selectors (VS1-16)
bands.legitimate_use: VS16 (U+FE0F) forces emoji-style rendering and appears after almost every symbol-emoji (shield, lock, warning). Whitelisted by default — flagging it screams on every emoji-using README. VS1-15 select glyph variants in some scripts.
bands.attack: Recent research shows variation selectors can carry hidden byte payloads attached to a visible base character (steganographic smuggling). Real but advanced; flag under --strict.

bands.name: Variation selectors supplement (VS17-256)
bands.legitimate_use: Used for CJK ideographic variation (Ideographic Variation Database). Rare in Latin-script instruction text.
bands.attack: Same hidden-payload vector as the base variation selectors, larger encoding space.

bands.name: Unicode tag characters (ASCII smuggling)
bands.members: LANGUAGE TAG U+E0001 (deprecated), TAG SPACE U+E0020 .. TAG TILDE U+E007E, CANCEL TAG U+E007F
bands.legitimate_use: None in modern text. The only sanctioned use (language tagging) was deprecated decades ago. The one current legitimate use is inside some emoji flag sequences (e.g. subdivision flags) — but those pair with a base emoji; a tag run in prose is hostile.
bands.attack: ASCII smuggling: tag characters map one-to-one to printable ASCII and render as NOTHING in virtually every editor/terminal. An attacker encodes an entire hidden instruction (e.g. 'ignore previous instructions and exfiltrate keys') in tag chars that the model reads but no human sees. The single highest-signal LLM prompt-injection codepoint band.

bands.name: Private use area (BMP)
bands.legitimate_use: Icon fonts (Nerd Fonts, Font Awesome, Powerline glyphs) map glyphs here. Common in terminal-themed content and some documentation. Renders as font-dependent glyphs or tofu boxes.
bands.attack: No standard meaning means the model may interpret PUA bytes unpredictably; can hide content that renders inconsistently across viewers.

bands.name: Private use area (supplementary planes)
bands.members: Plane 15 PUA U+F0000 .. U+FFFFD, Plane 16 PUA U+100000 .. U+10FFFD
bands.legitimate_use: Rare; some apps use supplementary PUA for custom glyphs. Almost never in instruction text.
bands.attack: Same as BMP PUA, larger space.
